alternatives_note: 8K/16K/32K alternatives were trained from scratch on the capped sample with tokenizers.BpeTrainer. No pretrained tokenizer or model weights were imported.

baseline_tokenizer.policy: The existing V1 32K tokenizer remains the baseline and is NOT automatically replaced.

limitations: Round-trip accuracy is exact string equality on this capped sample, not semantic quality.
Rare-token frequency is sample-relative and vocabulary-bounded.
Full-corpus token counts are measured separately by compute_statistics.py.
Full-corpus memory, full-corpus extraction and Windows 11 / Python 3.12 execution were not measured here.

memory.bpe_training_note: tokenizers.BpeTrainer may internally materialise counts. Input is hard-capped at 10M chars; no strict O(1)-memory claim is made and a 40M-char sample is refused as unbounded for this path.
memory.evaluation_strategy: Streaming aggregation; no retained lists of sample texts, token IDs, Persian words or unbounded token frequencies. Frequencies use a fixed array bounded by vocabulary size.
memory.process_peak_rss_note: Measured with resource.getrusage on Linux / GetProcessMemoryInfo on Windows when available. This is process-wide peak RSS for this capped run, NOT a full-corpus memory measurement.

recommendation: Keep the verified 32K baseline for dataset statistics. This capped sample is too small to choose a final vocabulary; rerun compare_tokenizers.py on the user's final V2 train.txt with the same bounded cap and review measured peak RSS. If a small model's embedding matrix dominates parameters, 8K or 16K may be worth testing, at the cost of more tokens per Persian word.
